newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: U.S. fugitive leaves Caymans for Jamaica - police.
newsitem.headline: U.S. fugitive leaves Caymans for Jamaica - police.

text.p: A U.S. fugitive has apparently fled to Jamaica after Cayman Island authorities waited in vain for an extradition warrant from the United States, officials said on Tuesday.
Royal Cayman Islands Police Chief Geoff Hall said Pat Luthra, 46, of Monroeville, Pennsylvania, had likely slipped out of this British territory in a stolen boat that was found in Jamaica.

Cayman authorities had learned that Luthra was wanted by the FBI on charges of stealing $700,000 from her former employer. They contacted prosecutors in Pittsburgh, but were told Luthra would be arrested if she turned up in Miami and that extradition would not be sought, he said.
"We had no cause to arrest her and she was allowed to remain free, even though I knew she was wanted in the States," he said.

Luthra worked as an accountant and bookkeeper for American Jewelry Manufacturing Corp of Monroeville and allegedly forged checks totalling more than $700,000 before fleeing Pennsylvania about a year ago, Hall said.
Hall said Luthra, who had worked in the Cayman Islands also as an accountant for several months, left her apartment last week, telling her roommate she would not be back.
On Thursday, a 30-foot boat was stolen from a beach on the east coast of Grand Cayman. Two days later, it was found in Runaway Bay on the west coast of Jamaica.
Hall said he had reason to believe the woman made her escape in the boat.
Three weeks ago Luthra's husband, Prem, travelled to Miami and was arrested by the FBI at the airport. "She obviously heard about her husband's arrest and made her plans accordingly," Hall said.
